Header: Mycosphaerella musicola Sinhala: Kola-pulli Rogaya; Tamil: Sigatoka Nooi

Prevention: Use proper spacing in order to avoid mutual shading and the contact of leaves (8 to 12 ft)
Keep an appropriate distance (100 – 500ft) between new plantations and disease-affected existing plantations
Establish live wind barriers around the field (eg.
Avoid surface irrigation / sprinkler irrigation to minimize the relative humidity of micro environment.
Avoid high density planting methods for highly susceptible cultivars (e.g.
Cavendish) and high risk areas (e.g. some down south areas)
Allow fields to dry as soon as possible just after rain by improving drainage / runoff
Keep minimum or no weed cover
Monitoring: Regular visits to the farm to identify the characteristic small yellow lesions parallel to veins towards the leaf margin in lower most leaves
Check for drying out of leaf margins (in severe cases)
If the fourth leaf from the bottom is infected, chemical control measures should be applied
Direct Control: Remove infected leaves and burn them
Field sanitation by removing old dried hanging leaves
Alternate spraying of a contact fungicide and a systemic fungicide
Restrictions: Fungicides are sprayed only during epidemic conditions.
